name: Multi-view batch navigation always saves, ignoring the Auto-Save setting
answer:
ANSWERED BY DECISIONS 7 AND 8 TOGETHER, and the second is what makes it simple.

Decision 8, approved: rebuild multi-view as a synchronized split view from the linked-operation rules, and DELETE the half-migrated legacy path rather than porting it. So the question - should multi-view honour Auto-Save on Navigate and the border crop like single view? - is answered yes, not by adding two behaviours to the legacy path but by there being one save path for every view.

Under decision 7 that path is explicit save with dirty tracking. It does not silently save on every navigation, it does not ignore the user's setting, and it does not delete a viewer image's annotation files because that viewer happened to be empty - which is what the legacy path does today, unconditionally, on every pair change.

THE DELETION CLAUSE IS THE DANGEROUS ONE and deserves naming separately from the Auto-Save question. In two-viewer mode, moving to the next pair deletes ALL annotation files of a viewer image that has no segments, every time, regardless of the setting. A user who opens a pair to look at it, and moves on without drawing, destroys the annotations of any image that lands in a viewer while empty. Decision 7 removes delete-on-empty everywhere; this is the place it costs the most.

The crop half follows for free: one save path applies the crop the same way in every view, so the card's 'without applying any crop' divergence has nowhere to live.

Scheduling: the split view itself is Phase 6 (decision 8), and its per-viewer class-id space is a Phase 6 entry decision. What Phase 4 owes this rule is that the single save path it builds is the one the split view will later call, rather than a single-view path that Phase 6 has to fork.
